blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At the executive level, a supply chain stops being a sequence of activities and becomes an architecture — a deliberate set of choices about where things are made, where they are stored, how far they travel, which risks are absorbed and which are passed on. The architecture shapes not just how the business delivers today, but how resilient it will be when the world around it changes.

The questions at this level are fewer and larger than at the operational level. How concentrated is production? How long are the lead times, and what does that cost us in working capital? Where are the single points of failure, and what would it take to remove them? Which parts of the chain are we running for cost, and which for resilience? These are not supply chain questions — they are strategy questions that happen to land on the supply chain desk.

The senior leader's task is to keep the architecture visible, review it regularly, and resist the natural drift toward silent concentration and hidden risk that years of optimisation always produce.

items.q: According to the text, what does a supply chain become at the executive level?
items.why: "a supply chain stops being a sequence of activities and becomes an architecture — a deliberate set of choices".

items.q: How does the text characterise the questions asked at the executive level?
options: Fewer and larger than at the operational level
items.why: "The questions at this level are fewer and larger than at the operational level."

items.q: The text says the big questions "happen to land on the supply chain desk." This suggests that…
options: they are fundamentally strategy questions, not narrow logistics ones
they are trivial and can be delegated downwards
the supply chain team should answer them alone
the supply chain desk is the wrong place for any decision
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz explicitamente que são 'strategy questions' — a mesa de supply chain é só onde elas pousam.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: If nothing has broken, the architecture needs no regular review.
Lead-time decisions carry a working-capital cost.
Resilience should be designed into the architecture from the start.
Years of optimisation can quietly concentrate risk.
items.why: Inferência: o autor defende revisar a arquitetura regularmente justamente porque o risco se acumula em silêncio, sem quebrar nada visível.

items.q: What does the phrase "natural drift toward silent concentration" imply about optimisation?
options: Its efficiency gains can hide a build-up of risk
Concentration is announced clearly to leadership
It is impossible to optimise a supply chain
items.why: Inferência: 'silent' e 'hidden risk' indicam que a busca por eficiência concentra o risco sem alarde, sem que ninguém perceba.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James conduzindo a revisão de conselho. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thank you all for making the time. What I want us to look at today is not a set of numbers — it is the shape of the supply chain itself. Over the last five years we have optimised, quarter after quarter, and each individual decision was sensible. The trouble is what those decisions add up to.

We have found three single points of failure that nobody chose deliberately. One supplier now makes ninety per cent of a critical component. One port handles almost everything we move out of Asia. And one system — with one person who understands it — reconciles the whole thing. None of that appears on a risk register, because each step looked efficient on its own.

I am not here to blame the optimisation. It did exactly what we asked of it: it took out cost. But cost was the only thing we ever measured, so resilience quietly drained away while nobody was watching.

So here is what I am proposing. From this year, we review the architecture at board level once every six months. We name every single point of failure, we put a number on what removing it would cost, and we decide — with open eyes — which risks we keep and which we pay to remove.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does James say the board should focus on today?
options: The shape of the supply chain itself
items.why: "it is the shape of the supply chain itself."

items.q: How many single points of failure did James's team find, and how did they arise?
options: One, caused by a supplier bankruptcy
Three, none of which anybody chose deliberately
Three, all chosen deliberately by the board
Several, all listed on the risk register
items.why: "We have found three single points of failure that nobody chose deliberately."

items.q: Why does James say none of the risks appeared on a risk register?
options: Because the board refused to record them
Because the suppliers hid the information
Because each individual step looked efficient on its own
Because the register was never updated
items.why: "None of that appears on a risk register, because each step looked efficient on its own."

items.q: What does James mean when he says "resilience quietly drained away while nobody was watching"?
options: The supply chain collapsed suddenly overnight
The team deliberately removed all safeguards
Because only cost was measured, resilience eroded unnoticed
Resilience was never a company goal
items.why: Inferência: medir só custo deixou a resiliência corroer sem que ninguém a monitorasse — não foi uma decisão explícita.

items.q: What is James's attitude toward the optimisation of the past five years?
options: He wants to reverse every decision it produced
He blames it entirely for the company's problems
He praises it as flawless and wants more of it
He accepts it did its job, but wants resilience measured too
items.why: Inferência: 'I am not here to blame the optimisation… it took out cost' — ele reconhece o valor, mas quer medir também a resiliência.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Every sourcing choice was deliberate, weighed against its risk." A deliberate choice is…
items.why: Deliberate = deliberado, feito de propósito e com intenção.

items.q: "A resilient chain keeps delivering even when a supplier fails." Resilient means…
options: able to recover from shocks and keep functioning
items.why: Resilient = resiliente, capaz de absorver choques e continuar operando.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Long ___ tie up cash in inventory, raising our working capital."
items.why: Lead time = prazo total; prazos longos prendem capital em estoque.

items.q: A single point of failure is best described as…
options: a supplier that offers the lowest price
the most profitable part of the chain
one node whose failure would bring the whole system down
items.why: É um ponto único cuja falha derruba o sistema inteiro — o risco central da lição.

items.q: "Production had quietly become dangerously concentrated in one region." Concentrated here means…
items.why: Concentrated = concentrado, reunido em poucos pontos — o oposto de diversificado.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem numa revisão de arquitetura de supply chain. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board must sign off on any change to the architecture." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the second supplier region by region." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "The plant manager pushed back on the dual-sourcing plan." He…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "They agreed to diversify but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado — aqui, não levaram.

items.q: "Trimming a few days off delivery won't move the needle on our risk exposure." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível — aqui, não faz.
